**Question:** Does the existing speed expectation — a 100,000-line log redacted in under 30 seconds — also have to hold when the output goes to a folder instead of standard output? (SC-007, SC-018)

**Why it matters:** `--out-dir` is aimed at batches of rotated logs, which is the largest input the tool will ever see. The spec pins memory use for those runs but says nothing about speed, so there is currently no criterion that would catch an implementation that reopens or re-reads files per line and takes minutes on a batch a plain run handles in seconds.

**Suggested:** Yes — the same 30-second budget per 100,000 lines applies, measured across all FILE operands together. It reuses an already-agreed number rather than inventing a second one, and it is the weakest criterion that still fails an accidentally quadratic implementation.

Format: Short answer (<=5 words). You can accept the suggestion by saying "yes" or "suggested", or provide your own answer.
